statement: The modular five-cycle is a symmetric, loop-free red/blue coloring with no monochromatic triangle; injective vertex restrictions preserve this property.
scope_gap: Known R(3,3) lower-bound witness only. No R(3,3) upper bound or R(5,5) determination. Independent statement review pending.
next_step: Match every edge to examples/R33_C5.json; then generalize certificate replay to clique sizes s and t.

statement: All 16 bitmask families on the ground set {0,1}: if union-closed and containing a nonempty set, some element belongs to at least half the family. Includes elementwise union semantics and the existing tiny benchmark.
scope_gap: Only the two-element ground universe, encoded as Fin 16. No proof for arbitrary ground-set sizes, no novelty claim; independent scope review pending.
next_step: Prove a representation theorem for arbitrary extensional set families on Fin 2, then generalize counting and union semantics to Fin n.

statement: Soundness of decoding a directed-graph SAT assignment into a loop-free graph with minimum outdegree and absence of short directed cycles.
scope_gap: SAT search output alone is not a theorem. UNSAT requires a checked proof and a separately proved encoding completeness theorem.
next_step: Formalize graph semantics and assignment decoder before attempting the 18-vertex target.

statement: Every even 4 ≤ n ≤ 100 is a sum of two primes, via a least-prime witness table re-checked by the kernel against the comparator Hundred.Statements.Goldbach.Statement.
scope_gap: Known range only (verified to 4·10^18 in the literature); no bound on the least prime and no progress on the unrestricted conjecture. Independent statement review pending.
next_step: Connect the witness table to the lab goldbach certificate hash and add a downstream lemma that uses Statement.

statement: Explicit positive solutions of 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx) for every 2 ≤ n ≤ 100, re-checked by the kernel against Hundred.Statements.ErdosStraus.Statement.
scope_gap: Known range only; no parametric identity for a residue class. Independent statement review pending.
next_step: Formalise one classical parametric identity (n ≡ 3 mod 4) as a theorem quantified over all such n.

statement: The generic Fin-based and Nat-bitmask family models agree on all two-element family memberships, counts, frequencies, union closure, nonempty-member conditions and abundance. Explicitly pack arbitrary Boolean predicates on the four subset masks; transport the two-element theorem into the generic comparator and combine the separately proved k=1 and k=3 cases.
scope_gap: Elementary finite k=1..3 cases only. The model-equivalence and explicit family packing theorems are proved only for k=2; the k=3 case is supplied independently, not derived from k=2. No unrestricted Frankl theorem, and no independent scope review.
next_step: Extend the family packing and semantic bridge to k=3 or to a uniform Fin (2^k) representation; connect genuine families of subsets of Fin k, not only the bitmask model.

statement: Explicit Hadamard matrices of orders 4, 8 (Sylvester) and 12 (Paley I, q = 11), re-checked by the kernel against Hundred.Statements.Hadamard.IsHadamard.
scope_gap: Small known orders only; the smallest open order is 668. Independent statement review pending.
next_step: Prove Sylvester doubling as a general theorem (order n to 2n) instead of instance by instance.

statement: ¬ Arrows 5 3 3 in the general clique encoding of Hundred.Statements.Ramsey (cliques as vertex bitmasks), so the R(5,5) comparator Conjecture := Arrows 43 5 5 is stated in a vocabulary with a checked witness.
scope_gap: Same known R(3,3) lower bound as L001 in a second, independent encoding. Exoo's K42 colouring and the 46 upper bound are cited, not re-proved. Independent statement review pending.
next_step: Prove the two Ramsey encodings agree on triangles (L001 TriangleFree vs HasMonoClique with s = 3).

statement: Projective planes of orders 2 and 3 satisfy the axioms in Hundred.Statements.ProjectivePlane.IsPlane, so the order-12 comparator is not vacuous.
scope_gap: Satisfiability of the axioms only; says nothing about order 12. Independent statement review pending.
next_step: Formalise the Bruck–Ryser condition as a checkable criterion and verify it for small orders.
